chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
The person in ihsar (ritual consecration) offers the ransom for the game from wherever it is found.
ai.seo_question: Where should the ransom for game be slaughtered if a person in ihram kills it?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar to establish the geographical scope of the ransom (fidyah) for game killed during Umrah. The ruling that the offering must be sourced 'from where it was found' underscores the principle of localizing the sacrificial obligation to the immediate vicinity of the ihram state, a view supported by Shia jurists to ensure the fidyah is accessible and contextually appropriate to the pilgrim's location.
